name: SLN
description: SLN returns the constant depreciation amount for each period using the straight-line method.
tldr: Calculates straight-line depreciation of an asset for one period.

parameters.name: salvage
parameters.description: Value at the end of the depreciation life.

parameters.name: life
parameters.description: Number of periods over which the asset is depreciated.

basicExample.explanation: A $10,000 asset with a $2,000 salvage value and 5-year life depreciates $1,600 per year.

howItWorks: SLN subtracts salvage value from cost and divides the result by the asset life. This gives the same depreciation amount every period.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Does not account for accelerated depreciation methods.
Life must be in the same units as the desired output (years, months, etc.).

commonErrors.fix: Ensure life is greater than zero.

commonErrors.cause: Salvage value is greater than cost.
commonErrors.fix: Verify that salvage value is less than or equal to cost.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SLN works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between SLN and SYD?
faq.answer: SLN uses straight-line depreciation. SYD uses sum-of-years-digits accelerated depreciation.

faq.question: Can SLN produce fractional periods?
faq.answer: No, SLN returns the same amount for each full period.
